sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper right. It covers the business centre of West Englewood around the junction of Queen Anne Road (Westfield Avenue) and West Englewood Avenue. Along the top runs Palisade Avenue, marked not open on its western part, and Station, which runs beside the West Shore railroad station area of the adjoining sheet. West Englewood Avenue crosses the sheet vertically and is lined north of Queen Anne Road with one- and two-storey stores of concrete block and tile: a post office, a bakery, auto repair shops, a bank and offices, with street numbers 166 to 212 and 181 to 193. West of it lie the large undivided blocks 249-N and 249-O between Bogert and Court. South of Queen Anne Road the sheet is residential: frame dwellings with garages along Bogert, Elm Terrace and the west side of West Englewood Avenue, an auto repairing garage of cinder block built from plans, and block 458 between West Englewood Avenue and Walraven Avenue, which is marked not open. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes run in most streets. The scale of feet and the copyright line are printed at the bottom, and the numbers of adjoining sheets 10, 14, 17 and 5 are shown at the margins.
notes: Elm Terrace is now Laurel Terrace; Walraven Avenue is Walraven Drive; Bogert and Court are Bogert Street and Court Street.
Station, along the top right, is the line of today's Palisade Avenue east of West Englewood Avenue.
Commercial centre: post office, bank, bakery and auto repair shops on West Englewood Avenue.

50 ft, turned (north upper right, about 63 deg). West Englewood business centre: Queen Anne Rd (Westfield Av) / West Englewood Av, Palisade Av and Station at top, Bogert, Court, Elm Ter (= Laurel Terrace), Walraven Av (= Walraven Drive). One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It covers the district between Bogert at the left edge and Walraven Avenue at the right, from the top of the sheet down to Teaneck Road, which crosses the bottom as a long diagonal. West Englewood Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and Orchard and Graham Place lie to its west, with Mersereau Terrace and Hill as the cross streets. Along the left edge the narrow lots of Bogert are filled with one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages, and Alicia Avenue, Beaumont Avenue and Longfellow Avenue open off it as water-pipe lines running in from the margin. The blocks between Bogert and West Englewood Avenue are only partly built, many of the lots standing vacant. East of West Englewood Avenue a few dwellings stand along the street in blocks 458 and 459, and near the lower right a large brick building of four storeys, lettered as apartments, with fire escapes and a courtyard, fills most of a block beside Teaneck Road. A tract of ground along the north side of Teaneck Road near Orchard is coloured blue and pink and carries lot numbers 1318 to 1368. Garden Street and Beveridge Street are lettered where they run in from Teaneck Road at the bottom. Six- and eight-inch water mains are drawn in the streets. A scale bar and the Princeton University Library map division stamp sit in the lower right margin, with the sheet title and oval stamp for West Englewood, N.J., Upper Teaneck at the top right.
notes: Bogert is now Bogert Street, Orchard is Orchard Street, Hill is Hill Street, Walraven Avenue is Walraven Drive.
Alicia, Beaumont and Longfellow avenues are drawn only as water-pipe lines running in from the left margin; the street edges are not drawn on this sheet.
50 ft, turned. Bogert, Orchard, Graham Pl, Mersereau Ter, West Englewood Av, Walraven Av, Hill, Teaneck Rd, Garden St, Beveridge St; large brick apartment building in block 459. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It covers the area from Katherine at the top to Arlington Avenue at the bottom, and from Selvage Avenue at the left to Church at the right. Teaneck Road crosses the upper half of the sheet as a long diagonal. Above it, along Katherine, a row of narrow lots is lined with one- and two-storey frame dwellings. To the right, Teaneck Public School No. 2 (block 433) is a large brick and frame building, with a smaller vacant school building east of it near Church. Along the south side of Teaneck Road stand rows of one-storey brick and frame stores, numbered 1118 to 1128 near Selvage Avenue, with a drug store, and 1201 to 1213 further east, including a bakery, a battery service station and Teaneck Fire Company No. 1. St. Anatasia's R.C. Church stands between Selvage Avenue and Prospect Street, and a compass arrow is drawn in the same block. Parkway Avenue runs across the middle of the sheet. South of it the sheet is laid out as long blocks between Robinson, Prospect Terrace South, Prospect Terrace North, Forest Avenue and Fairview Avenue (blocks 419, 420, 431, 435), only partly built, with frame dwellings and garages along the street frontages and much vacant ground. Arlington Avenue closes the sheet at the bottom. Six- and eight-inch water mains are lettered in most streets. A scale bar stands at the lower left, and the sheet title and stamp for West Englewood, N.J., Upper Teaneck are at the top right.
notes: Parkway Avenue is now Overlook Avenue; Forest Avenue is West Forest Avenue; Katherine is Katherine Street; Robinson is Robinson Street; Church is Church Street; Prospect Terrace South and North are South and North Prospect Terrace.
St. Anatasia's R.C. Church is lettered as printed on the sheet.
Arlington Avenue junctions were hand-picked on the water-pipe line; the detector had locked onto lot lines about 45 ft to the north.

Church. Arlington row (south side not drawn) hand-picked. Fitted px_per_ft 1.7 percent above sheet 5. One part.

sheet-13-1.description: Main part of sheet 13 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It spans from Carlton Terrace on the left to Selvage Avenue on the right, between Queen Anne Road (Westfield Avenue) at the top and Teaneck Road at the bottom. The middle of the sheet is taken up by the grounds of Teaneck High School, a fireproof building of 1928 with manual training rooms, cafeteria, auditorium and gymnasium, with Cranford Place running down its west side marked not opened. To the right, Elizabeth Avenue (Parker) bounds a partly built area, and between it and Selvage Avenue the cross streets Julia, Margaret, Alicia Avenue (Julia), Stasia, Anna and Katherine are closely built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, as are King Court and Colonial Court, two short cul-de-sacs off Queen Anne Road. At the upper left, Carlton Terrace, Grayson Place and Cranford Place carry new dwellings, many marked from plans, with Red Road, Edgemont Terrace, Ridge Way and Prince below them. Along Teaneck Road stand scattered dwellings, sheds and the Rosemaid Corp. ladies garment factory; Stevenson Lane leads off it. The lower left corner, inside a heavy line, is a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Julia, Margaret, Stasia, Anna and Katherine are now Julia Street, Margaret Street, Stasia Street, Anna Street and Katherine Street; Prince is Prince Street; Ridge Way is Ridgeway Street.
Teaneck High School, built 1928.
Rosemaid Corp., ladies garments, on Teaneck Road.

sheet-13-2.description: Inset in the lower left corner of sheet 13 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), set off by a heavy line and drawn at the sheet's 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing to the upper right. It shows a short stretch of Teaneck Road south of the main map, at Golf Court and Fairway Avenue, two short streets running off its east side. On the corner of Teaneck Road and Golf Court stands a two-storey dance hall, and between Golf Court and Fairway Avenue a two-storey store and office building; a few dwellings with garages lie in blocks 742, 743 and 744. An eight-inch water pipe runs along Teaneck Road. The inset has only one usable junction, Golf Court and Teaneck Road, so its placement rests on that point and the assumed scale.
notes: Anchored on Golf Court / Teaneck Road with the scale of sheet 14 and the rotation from its drawn lines; low confidence.
Fairway Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It covers the residential district between Queen Anne Road (Westfield Avenue) at the top and Teaneck Road at the bottom, from Selvage Avenue on the left to Bogert on the right. Forest Avenue and Church run down the sheet, with Pinewood Place and Evergreen Place to the east. West of Forest Avenue the cross streets Julia, Margaret, Alicia Avenue (Julia), Stasia, Anna and Katherine are almost completely built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages, numbered 1131 to 1176. East of Church the streets are Alicia Avenue, Beaumont Avenue and Longfellow (Hazelton) Avenue, also largely built. St. Paul's Lutheran Church stands on Church at Beaumont Avenue, and the Presbyterian Church of Teaneck near Teaneck Road, with a large building beside it in block 433. Linwood Avenue, Church Street, Kendall Place and Pinewood Place are lettered at the top margin. Below Teaneck Road a strip shows Fairview Avenue, Circle Driveway and Bedford Avenue running down to Parkway Avenue, with Genesee Avenue at the corner. Six- and eight-inch water pipes run in most streets.
notes: Forest Avenue is now West Forest Avenue; Circle Driveway is Circle Drive; Parkway Avenue is Overlook Avenue.
St. Paul's Lutheran Church and the Presbyterian Church of Teaneck.
Evergreen Place / Queen Anne Road was rejected (16 m).

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It covers the south-western part of Upper Teaneck, from Stevenson Lane at the left to Bedford Avenue at the right, and from Parkway Avenue at the top down to Loraine Avenue and the City of Englewood line at the bottom. A grid of cross streets, Arlington Avenue, Summit Avenue, Congress Avenue, Tuxedo Square, Madison Avenue and Cooper Avenue, is crossed by Robinson, Prospect Terrace, Forest Avenue and Fairview Avenue. East of Fairview Avenue, Circle Driveway and Bedford Avenue run down the sheet, and two traffic circles are drawn on Circle Driveway, one at Parkway Avenue and one near Cooper Avenue. The blocks (numbered 400 to 444 and 526 to 534) are divided into narrow lots, most of them still vacant; the buildings are scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages, with a short row of dwellings along Fairview Avenue and a cluster of stores and an auto repair shop on Forest Avenue. The top left of the sheet is largely blank, with a large building near Stevenson Lane. Along the bottom, the Loraine Avenue strip is drawn at a slant: Tietjen Avenue, Thomson Avenue and Rosemont Place run down to the dash-dot line marked City of Englewood, below which lie blocks 528 E to 528 H and 530. A scale bar for 100 feet to an inch and the copyright line stand at the bottom. Six-inch water mains are lettered in most streets.
notes: Parkway Avenue is now Overlook Avenue; Forest Avenue is East Forest Avenue; Circle Driveway is Circle Drive; Loraine Avenue is Lorraine Avenue; Thomson Avenue is Thompson Avenue; Robinson is Robinson Street.
The Tietjen Avenue lettering is hard to read; the reading follows the modern street name.
Stevenson Lane is not in the modern street data and was not used as control.
The City of Englewood boundary is drawn as a dash-dot line near the bottom.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Teaneck Road crosses the top of the sheet as a diagonal, with Bogert St., Orchard St., West Englewood Avenue, Beveridge and Westervelt Place running down from it. The upper left blocks, between Bogert St. and Garden and along Franklin Rd., are narrow lots filled with regular rows of one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages numbered up to 1367. Byng crosses below them, and the lower middle of the sheet, blocks 452, 462, 464 and 465 between Genesee Avenue and Hirliman Rd., is almost entirely vacant, with a compass arrow and the library stamp in the blank ground. A strip of long, narrow lots at the left edge, blocks 445 to 449 and 533, lies between Bedford Avenue and Genesee Avenue, with Liberty, Franklin St., Arlington Av., Hobson Pl., Putnam, Tuxedo Sq. and Madison Av. (Palisade) crossing it. On the right, Van Duyn Pl., Hubert Ter., Basil and Pine Ter. open off Schoonmaker Rd. and Hirliman Rd.; Hubert Ter. and Basil bend round curved, fan-shaped lot layouts in blocks 535 and 523, and a few dwellings stand along Pine Ter. and Spruce in blocks 536 and 537. The Englewood Sanitarium, a long two-storey frame building with a brick wing, stands at the right edge in block 468, with heat by steam and hot water, electric light and a day and night watchman, and a burnt building marked as fire ruins nearby. A few dwellings stand around Acton Pl. in blocks 466 and 467 near the top. A scale bar for 100 feet to an inch stands at the bottom.
notes: Beveridge is now Beveridge Street; Garden is Garden Street; Byng is Byng Street; Franklin Road is unchanged; Van Duyn Place, Hirliman Road, Schoonmaker Road and Hubert Terrace keep their names.
Madison Avenue is lettered with Palisade in brackets.
The Englewood Sanitarium is a named institution; a burnt building is marked fire ruins.
Liberty, Franklin Street, Hobson Place, Putnam and Basil have no matching street in the modern data and were not used as control.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Across the top runs the New York Central (West Shore) railroad with the West Englewood station and a concrete bridge carrying a street over the tracks, with Windsor Road beyond and a stream crossing the blocks north of the line. Station runs along the south side of the tracks, with the West Englewood Coal and Supply Co. yard. Below, the sheet is mostly laid out but still empty: Walraven Avenue (not opened), Market, State and Ackerman Avenue (not opened) run down the sheet with State Court and Market Court between them, and Queen Anne Road (Westfield Avenue), Hill and Lozier cross them. A curved bank building of tile and stores stands on Queen Anne Road at the top left, and the West Englewood Apartments of 1929 on Lozier. To the right Amsterdam Avenue and Tryon Avenue frame blocks with a few new dwellings, and Irving Place curves between them. Along Teaneck Road at the bottom are filling stations, a battery service, apartments, stores and an auto repair garage, with Westervelt Place, Englewood Avenue, Shepard Avenue, Washington Place and Gramercy Place leading off it.
notes: Station is now Palisade Avenue; Irving Place is now part of Queen Anne Road; Walraven Avenue is Walraven Drive; Lozier is Lozier Place; Tryon Avenue is West Tryon Avenue.
West Englewood station on the West Shore railroad; West Englewood Coal and Supply Co.; West Englewood Apartments, 1929.
The 1929 Queen Anne Road segment at State was rejected (11.6 m) against today's Queen Anne Road.

sheet-18-1.description: Main part of sheet 18 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. The West Shore railroad crosses the top of the sheet, with Station Street at the left and paper blocks north of the tracks on Grafton, Wall, Quincy Lane, Pearl, Vesey and Nassau. Below the railroad, Tryon Avenue runs down the left side, and Bilton and Sackville enclose the small blocks of Dame, Stephen and Shelbourne, mostly vacant lots with a few dwellings. Teaneck Road crosses the sheet diagonally. South of it a regular subdivision of long narrow lots is laid out on Gramercy Place, Intervale Road, Van Buskirk Road, Hamilton Road, Voorhees, Stuyvesant Road, Irvington Place (Road) and Van Arsdale Place, cut by Van Cortland Terrace; the western blocks are partly built with frame dwellings and the eastern ones still empty. Public School No. 6 stands between Tryon Avenue and Teaneck Road, and Tunis and Library lead off Teaneck Road at the right. The upper right corner, inside a heavy line, is an inset (part 2).
notes: Bilton, Sackville and Shelbourne are now Bilton Street, Sackville Street and Shelbourne Street; Stephen appears to be the northern arm of today's Shelbourne Street; Irvington Place is Irvington Road; Van Cortland Terrace is Van Cortlandt Terrace; Voorhees is Voorhees Street.

sheet-18-2.description: Inset in the upper right of sheet 18 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), set off by a heavy box and drawn with its own north arrow. It shows the junction of Van Arsdale Place and Van Cortland Terrace with Irvington Place below, and the yard of the West Englewood Lumber Co. with a raised lumber storage shed and a lumber shed in block 556. The blocks marked 18 belong to the main part of the sheet. The inset has two street junctions, so it is placed by position, scale and rotation only.
notes: Helmert fit on two junctions; its own scale came out 16 percent below the atlas value, so the inset is low confidence.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 of the March 1929 West Englewood volume (Upper Teaneck), drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It covers the south-eastern corner of Upper Teaneck, from Teaneck Road at the top left down to the Teaneck Township and City of Englewood boundary line at the bottom, and from Englewood Avenue on the left to the Tryon Avenue and Gramercy Place diagonal on the right. Shepard Avenue, Howland Avenue, Washington Place and Manhattan Avenue run down the sheet as parallel streets, crossed by Gaylord, Endicott and Buffet terraces, Crescent Avenue, Berkley, Walden, a street lettered Swamp (Summer Av.) and East View. Between Englewood Avenue and Howland Avenue the blocks 471B and 471C are filled with a close regular grid of small frame dwellings, while the blocks along Shepard Avenue and Washington Place have one- and two-storey dwellings scattered on long narrow lots. Much of the middle of the sheet (blocks 471 to 472, 471D, 741) is vacant. A larger building lettered Apartments stands at the top near Tryon Avenue. On the right, Gramercy Place, Van Cortland Ter. (not open) and Tryon Avenue cut diagonally through long, mostly empty subdivision blocks (490, 549), with a compass arrow in the vacant ground to the east. At the bottom, Palisade, St. Marks Pl. and Ardsley Ct. run to the boundary line, below which the legend See Map of Englewood is printed and the sheet notes that a few buildings are also shown on the Englewood map. Six-inch water mains are lettered in most streets. A scale bar stands at the lower left.
notes: Berkley is now Berkeley Street; Walden is Walden Street; Buffet Terrace is Buffett Terrace; Van Cortland Terrace (not open) is Van Cortlandt Terrace; Tryon Avenue is East Tryon Avenue; Palisade is Palisade Avenue; East View is Eastview Avenue; St. Marks Place is St Marks Place in the modern data.
Swamp (Summer Av.), Pine Terrace and Belmont Street have no match in the modern street data.
A boundary line between Teaneck Township and the City of Englewood crosses the bottom of the sheet; ground below it is on the Englewood map.
Englewood Avenue at Spruce Street carries a residual of about 4.5 m.
